body.p: In the non-final Office Action', the Examiner rejected claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by the video game "Golden Eye 007" (hereinafter Golden Eye).
By this Amendment, Applicant amends claims 1-3, 5-6, 10-12, 14-15, and 19, and

cancels claim 20 without any prejudice and disclaimer of the subject matter thereof. Applicant further adds new claim 21 to address other aspects of the present invention. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the as-filed application, for example, in para. [0054] and [0096] of the specification. Upon entry of this Amendment, claims 1-19 and 21 remain pending and under examination.
Applicant respectfully requests that the Office favorably reconsider and withdraw the rejections, and timely allow the pending claims for at least the reasons set forth below.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for conducting the phone interview with the undersigned Applicant's representative on April 4, 2024, to discuss the amended claims and applied reference. Applicant appreciates the Examiner's suggestion to further modify the claim language. The Examiner agreed that after the modification, the amended claim 1 would overcome the rejections in the present Office Action.
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as
allegedly being anticipated by Golden Eye. However, to expedite the prosecution of the present application, Applicant amends independent claims 1, 10, and 19.

1 The Office Action contains a number of statements reflecting characterizations of the related art and the claims. Regardless of whether any such statement is identified herein, Applicant declines to automatically subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
As discussed during the interview, Applicant respectfully submits that Golden Eye fails to teach or suggest, at least the following
controlling, in response to a use instruction detected by the computer
device, a target virtual character to use an equipped first virtual item, the target virtual character being controlled by a player, and the first virtual
item being configured to temporarily disable an item belonging to the

p.u: target type located within a first influence range of the first virtual item;

body.p: displaying, in response to the second virtual item being located within
the first influence range of the first virtual item used by the target virtual character, that the second virtual item is switched from the effective state
to an ineffective state
as recited in amended claim 1 (emphasis added), and similar features in amended independent claims 10 and 19.

Golden Eye discloses a remote mine game where a player can throw a mine that can be detonated when contacted by a character. That is, Golden Eye merely suggests switching a single item (i.e., the mine) from disabled to enabled state based on game character, NOT disabling an item based on its location relationship with another item used by a player. Thus, Golden Eye fails to teach or suggest, at least, "the target virtual character being controlled by a player, the first virtual item being configured to temporarily disable an item belonging to the target type located within a first influence range of the first virtual item; displaying, in response to the second virtual item being located within the first influence range of the first virtual item used by the target virtual character, that the second virtual item is switched from the effective state to an ineffective state," as recited in amended claim 1 (emphases added).

In view of the above, Golden Eye fails to disclose each and every element of amended claim 1, and thus claim 1 and its dependent claims are not anticipated by Golden Eye. Amended independent claims 10 and 19, although different in scope, recite elements similar to those of amended claim 1. For at least reasons similar to those discussed above in regard to the rejection
of claim 1, independent claims 10 and 19, are not anticipated by Golden Eye either, as well as their dependent claims.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102.

Newly added claim 21 is allowable at least by virtue of its dependence from an allowable base claim, and on the merits of its own subject matter that is not disclosed in or suggested by the cited references.

In light of the above, Applicant respectfully requests Examiner's favorable consideration and timely allowance of all pending claims. If any issues may be resolved by telephone with the Applicant's representative, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the numbers shown.
Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account 505213.
